canonical_topic: Photovoltaic (PV) effect and solar cell operation
definition: PV power generation relies on sunlight striking a semiconductor and dislodging electrons, which can then be captured as electrical current.
core_idea: Photons hitting a semiconductor knock electrons out of their normal orbit (valence band) into a free-moving state (conduction band); wiring the semiconductor into a circuit turns that freed-electron field into usable current.
key_points: The 'band gap' is the energy threshold needed to knock an electron from the valence band into the conduction band.
Photons below the band gap energy pass through the semiconductor unabsorbed and contribute nothing.
Photons above the band gap free an electron; any energy in excess of the band gap is wasted as heat rather than converted to electricity.
Individual solar cells are small but are wired together into arrays (solar panels) to scale output.
relationships: Band gap mismatch with photon energy is a core source of PV inefficiency, motivating multi-layer cell designs.
caveats: Not all sunlight striking a panel is convertible — photons either too weak (pass through) or too strong (excess becomes heat) are both partly or fully wasted.
